title: Review: Codominance and multiple alleles; Chi-squared test; Pleiotropy and non-nuclear inheritance; Polygenic and environmental variation
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: IN06#t3 term and clue written for the game; IN07#t1 term and clue written for the game; IN09#t1 term and clue written for the game; IN06#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: IN02#N.11a, IN06#N.11, IN07#N.6b, IN09#N.8, IN02#N.4b, IN06#N.5b, IN09#N.3, IN09#N.9. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Genotype
items.clue: The set of alleles that an organism has.

items.label: Pleiotropy
items.clue: The expression of one gene produces several traits or effects.

items.label: Critical value
items.clue: Figure looked up at p = 0.05, against which the calculated statistic is compared.

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, a cross of red-flowered plants with white-flowered plants produced only pink-flowered plants. A student claims that flower colour is controlled by one gene with two incompletely dominant alleles, so that pink-flowered plants are heterozygous. Which result of crossing pink-flowered plants with white-flowered plants would best support the student's claim?

options.text: About one red-flowered : two pink-flowered : one white-flowered
Offspring all of one shade, paler than the pink-flowered parents
About equal numbers of pink-flowered and white-flowered offspring
Pink-flowered offspring only, as each gamete carries both its alleles

questions.stem: In tomatoes, purple stems (A) are dominant to green stems (a). An Aa plant is crossed with an aa plant. Of 200 seedlings, 115 are purple and 85 are green (illustrative data). Critical values at p = 0.05: 3.84 for 1 degree of freedom, 5.99 for 2. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: χ² = 4.5; with two classes there are 2 degrees of freedom, so 4.5 < 5.99 and the difference is not significant.
χ² = 4.5, which is above 3.84, so the data fit the 1 : 1 ratio well.
χ² = 4.5, which is above 3.84, so the difference is significant: reject the null hypothesis of 1 : 1.
Reject the null hypothesis, because 115 and 85 are not exactly 100 each.

questions.stem: Arctic foxes grow brown fur in summer and white fur in winter. Which statement best explains how one fox can produce both fur colours?

options.text: Winter cold causes mutations in its fur-colour genes each year, and these mutations reverse in summer.
The fox decides to grow white fur each winter because it needs camouflage in the snow.
Its genotype stays the same, but seasonal changes in its environment change gene expression in its fur cells.
Each winter, natural selection removes foxes with brown-fur alleles, so the foxes turn white.

questions.stem: A researcher suspects that a trait of reduced swimming endurance in a hypothetical species of fish is determined by mitochondrial DNA. She has true-breeding lines of fish with the trait and without it. Which crossing design would best test whether the trait is maternally inherited?

options.text: Females with the trait × males without it, and females without it × males with it
Females with the trait × males without it, and females without it × males without it
Females with the trait × males without it, with only the sons of this cross scored
Females with the trait × males without it, repeated with a much larger number of pairs

questions.stem: In a hypothetical species of plant, flower colour is controlled by one gene with two alleles that show incomplete dominance. Plants homozygous for one allele have red flowers, and plants homozygous for the other allele have white flowers. Which description of the heterozygous plants' flowers is correct?

options.text: Each flower has separate red patches and white patches on its petals.
All of the flowers are one shade, such as pink, between red and white.
Some plants have red flowers and others have white, as dominance is incomplete.
Each flower is the colour produced by the more common allele in the population.

questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance neither allele masks the other, so every heterozygote has the same intermediate phenotype.

questions.stem: A student crosses two pea plants that are heterozygous for flower colour; the allele for purple flowers is dominant to the allele for white flowers. The student will perform a chi-square test on the numbers of purple-flowered and white-flowered offspring. Which is the appropriate null hypothesis?

options.text: Purple-flowered and white-flowered offspring will be found in equal numbers.
Offspring will be purple and white in a 3:1 ratio, apart from chance deviations.
The observed numbers will differ significantly from those expected for 3:1.
Exactly three-quarters of the offspring will be purple, with no variation at all.

questions.explanation: A chi-square null hypothesis states that observed counts differ from those expected from the genetic model only by chance. Pp × Pp predicts 3 purple : 1 white.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of pleiotropy?

options.text: Alleles of several genes add together to set the height of a plant.
One gene in a mouse affects both its coat colour and ear development.
Two genes close together on a chromosome are usually inherited together.
One gene in a rabbit has four alleles, giving four forms of coat colour.

questions.explanation: Pleiotropy is the expression of a single gene producing multiple traits or effects; here one gene affects two traits.

questions.stem: The pedigree shows the inheritance of a rare trait in a family. Which pattern of inheritance is most consistent with the pedigree, and why?

options.text: X-linked recessive, because the trait passes from affected mothers to their sons.
Autosomal dominant, because the trait appears in every generation of the family.
Mitochondrial, because affected mothers have affected children and affected fathers do not.
Autosomal recessive, because the trait is rare and is found in both males and females.

questions.explanation: All children of the affected mothers I-1 and II-4 are affected, sons and daughters, and neither child of the affected father II-2 is. Mitochondria are transmitted by the egg, so this is the mitochondrial pattern.
